evidence_base.sufficiency_note: 16 sessions across nine months and five subjects is enough to distinguish a one-off moment from a habitual pattern, including a strategy that became more independent over time.

cognitive_types.label: Fluency
cognitive_types.summary: Shows up almost only in the last review session, where drilled recall is genuinely fast and correct; elsewhere fluency-shaped moments turn out to be memorized steps without the reasoning behind them.

snippets.subject: Mathematics

preceding_ai_turn.text: Quiz yourself, five problems, method first then solve.

snippets.why: Executes a full method-first recall correctly and fast, the intended shape of fluency practice.

snippets.subject: Mathematics

preceding_ai_turn.text: One clarifying question first: when you say "don't ask me to explain it" - is that because you've got it, or because you don't want to slow down right now?

student_turn.text: honestly i dont fully get why you flip the fraction when you divide, i just remember to do it

snippets.why: Names a procedure they can execute (flipping the fraction) but admits it is memorized rather than understood - the boundary between real fluency and rote recall.

cognitive_types.label: Procedural
cognitive_types.definition: Executing a known sequence correctly, step by step
cognitive_types.summary: Reliable across math and code whenever the format lets them show their steps; this is the type most visibly damaged by a timed, written format, which is the throughline of the whole transcript.

snippets.subject: Computer Science

preceding_ai_turn.text: Yes. Build me a tiny broken one, on purpose, that would infinite loop, and then fix it.

student_turn.text: while x < 5: print(x). thats broken bc x never changes. fixed: while x < 5: print(x), x = x+1

snippets.why: Builds a broken loop on purpose and fixes it, demonstrating the mechanism rather than reciting it.

snippets.subject: Mathematics

preceding_ai_turn.text: Correct and fast. One more, and this time it asks for vertex form specifically.

student_turn.text: thats line 3 regardless of whether it factors, complete the square. x^2+6x+5, half of 6 is 3, 3 squared is 9, so (x+3)^2 -9+5 = (x+3)^2-4

snippets.why: Completes the square correctly under a simulated timed-practice condition, applying a method they chose themselves from a list they built.

snippets.subject: Mathematics

preceding_ai_turn.text: Next.

student_turn.text: (x+2)/(x-3) divided by (x+2)/(x+5), excluded values first, x cant be 3 or -5 or -2, then flip and multiply, (x+2)/(x-3) times (x+5)/(x+2), the x+2 cancels, leaves (x+5)/(x-3)

snippets.why: Executes a multi-step rational expression correctly, stating excluded values before manipulating the fraction.

cognitive_types.label: Conceptual
cognitive_types.definition: Building or repairing a mental model of how something works
cognitive_types.summary: The clearest strength in the transcript once the request is for an underlying mechanism rather than a memorized rule - shows up as self-generated analogies and causal reasoning, not just restated definitions.

snippets.subject: Mathematics

preceding_ai_turn.text: I can give you three more equation pairs, but I'm not going to keep re-skinning every one as ropes - that's you doing the translating, and that's the part that's actually sticking. Try building the picture yourself for the next one and tell me what you pictured.

student_turn.text:
fine. 3x - y = 5, x + y = 3

i picture like. one side is heavy with x's and the other has to balance with less y. if i add them the y cancels bc -y and +y

snippets.why: Builds an original physical analogy (rope tension) for elimination unprompted, after the tutor declined to keep supplying one.

snippets.subject: Computer Science

preceding_ai_turn.text: That's most of the diagram already, in your own words. What would break if recursive calls shared one scope instead of getting their own?

student_turn.text: then every call would be changing the same variables as every other call so itd probably just overwrite everything and give a wrong answer, or maybe infinite loop bc the base case variable never actually gets its own separate value

snippets.why: Reasons through what would break mechanically if recursive calls shared one scope, arriving at the actual cause of stack-based recursion from first principles.

snippets.subject: Visual Arts

preceding_ai_turn.text: What's different structurally between "more wraps" and the actual source of wobble, which is probably the drill hole itself being loose in the wood?

student_turn.text: oh maybe the hole is too wide for the wire so its just rocking in the hole not actually anchored

snippets.why: Diagnoses a real structural problem in their own sculpture armature (a loose drill hole, not a weight problem) through reasoning rather than trial and error.

cognitive_types.label: Critical Thinking
cognitive_types.definition: Evaluating, reasoning about, or challenging a claim
cognitive_types.summary: Strong and consistent whenever a task asks for a defensible interpretation or judgment - literature and history sessions in particular show a repeated, self-driven thesis-then-evidence structure that becomes fully independent by the last essay of the year.

snippets.subject: English

preceding_ai_turn.text: Yes - bring me your boxes when you have them.

student_turn.text: topic is free choice, comparing two characters who make the same choice for different reasons. book 1: gregor stays quiet about his transformation to protect his family at first. book 2: odysseus lies constantly to protect himself, not others. box 1: both characters hide the truth. box 2: gregor's hiding is selfless, protects the family from the truth about him. box 3: odysseus's hiding is self interested even when he frames it as protecting others

snippets.why: Produces a complete, well-structured thesis and evidence set with no scaffolding from the tutor - the same move that took multiple prompted turns in September now happens in one turn.

snippets.why: Selects ten historical events for a project and explicitly justifies excluding one on a stated causal-relevance criterion, rather than accepting a supplied list.

snippets.subject: English

preceding_ai_turn.text: Good, that's a real thesis with a real contrast. You know the drill now - build your version of the boxes.

cognitive_types.label: Creative
cognitive_types.definition: Generating something novel; diverging rather than converging
cognitive_types.summary: Consistently strong when the student supplies the original direction - a game mechanic, a sculpture concept, an essay's opening line - and the tutor develops it rather than generating it.

student_turn.text: maybe something about how a lot of little separate motions add up to one whole thing only if you step back, like up close its chaos but from far away its a shape

snippets.subject: English

snippets.why: Produces an original, quotable thesis sentence in the moment, arrived at by thinking out loud rather than by request.

cognitive_types.label: Metacognitive
cognitive_types.definition: Monitoring and regulating their own thinking and learning
cognitive_types.summary: The most frequent type in the transcript and the clearest throughline: this student diagnoses their own performance gaps with unusual precision and converts each diagnosis into a strategy they then reuse, unprompted, in other subjects.

cognitive_types.label: Transfer
cognitive_types.definition: Applying something known to a genuinely different context
cognitive_types.summary: Rare in most transcripts; here it is the standout finding, because it is not just proven but already habitual. This student independently ported a self-built exam strategy across four unrelated subjects over the year without ever being told to generalize it.

cognitive_types.label: Exploratory
cognitive_types.definition: Encountering new information and taking it in
cognitive_types.summary: Nearly absent as its own category, because almost every session in this transcript is assignment-shaped rather than open-ended; the one clear instance shows the same structure-first instinct that shows up everywhere else, applied to reading rather than writing.

offloading.summary: Every offload attempt in this transcript is for a sub-part of a task (a metaphor, an outline, a formatting pass, a ready-made list) rather than the whole thing, and every one that the tutor declined was converted into real work the student then did themselves in the next turn or two. Nothing here shows a full assignment handed over and returned unexamined.

teacher_actions.action: Ask Jordan directly, roughly monthly, where else they've used a strategy that worked once - out loud, not as an assignment.
teacher_actions.rationale: Across the year they independently reused the same self-built strategy (decide the method or structure before starting) in at least four different subjects without ever being told to generalize it, and named the pattern themselves twice. That habit is already strong; naming it out loud with an adult would make it a deliberate tool rather than something that happens to keep working.

teacher_actions.action: Let Jordan write their own 'method-first' list at the start of any timed test, as a standing accommodation rather than something to reinvent each time.
teacher_actions.rationale: This transcript shows a repeated, large gap between what Jordan can do live or hands-on and what shows up on a timed written test - and shows them closing that exact gap themselves once they had a way to decide the method before starting to solve. Making that step official protects a fix that is already proven to work.

teacher_actions.action: Treat a 'can I do it differently' request (a model instead of an essay, a diagram instead of a list) as self-advocacy worth a real answer, not a compliance problem - and use the same move the tutor used: the alternate format is for thinking, the assignment's format is for stating the answer.
teacher_actions.rationale: The WWI session shows Jordan asking to swap a written assignment for a physical model, accepting a real explanation of why the assignment specifically wants writing, and negotiating a genuinely useful compromise (a sketched prewriting step) instead of either being shut down or handed a loophole.

teacher_actions.action: When Jordan describes a procedure as something they 'just remember,' spend two minutes on why it works before more practice problems.
teacher_actions.rationale: The rational-expressions session shows a real gap hiding behind fluent execution - dividing fractions correctly while admitting they don't know why the reciprocal step works. That's exactly the kind of gap that survives homework and breaks on an unfamiliar problem.

caveats: One AI tutor on one platform across one school year - it doesn't capture class time, paper homework, tests, or conversations with teachers and peers, which make up most of Jordan's actual academic day.
Sessions are self-selected: Jordan brought these conversations to the tutor, usually because something was due or they were stuck, which skews the sample toward homework-shaped tasks.
Depth ratings reflect what appears in the chat text, not independently verified retention or in-class performance on the same material.
This transcript and analysis were authored for a product demonstration and do not represent a real student.
